 JUDGMENT

These two appeals and cross objection are arising out of common judgment and award dated MFA No.200653/2019 C/W 23.11.2018 in MVC Nos.57 & 58/2017 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Shahapur.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. MFA.No.200652/2016 is filed by respondent No.2 challenging compensation granted in MVC.No.57/2017 for the damage caused to the auto rickshaw.
4. MFA.No.200653/2016 is filed by petitioner seeking enhancement of compensation granted in M V C . N o .

5 8 / 2 0 1 7 i n r e s p e c t o f p e r s o n a l i n j u r i e s s u s t a i n e d b y h i m , w h e r e a s MFA.Crob.No.200001/2022 is filed by respondent No.2 challenging the said judgment and award.
5. In both MVC Nos.57 & 58/2017, petitioner and respondents are common.

MFA No.200653/2019 C/W 6. MVC No.57/2017 was filed seeking compensation for the damages caused to the auto rickshaw and MVC No.58/2017 was filed for recovery compensation for the personal injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident dated 26.05.2016.
7. Since these appeals are arising out of common judgment and award, they are clubbed together and disposed of by a common judgment.
8. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that he is the registered owner of auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-33/A-5843 ('auto rickshaw' for short).
On 26.01.2016,he was proceeding in the said auto rickshaw.

At round 2.00 p.m., when he came near Chatnalli cross, a KSRTC bearing The Managing Director Neksrtc vs Umesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74940625/
4 registration No.KA-32/F-1433 ('offending vehicle' for short) driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came from the opposite side and dashed against the auto rickshaw.

sentences.text: As a result of the accident, petitioner MFA No.200653/2019 C/W sustained injuries on his nose and also suffered fracture of leg bone.
He took treatment in the Government Hospital, Shahapur as well as Private Hospitals.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
In the said accident, the auto rickshaw was also extensively damaged.

As the driver and owner of the offending vehicle,
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

9. Respondents have appeared and filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation,
income of the petitioner, the cause of the accident and that in the said accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and that the auto rickshaw was also extensively damaged.
It is denied that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

10. On the other hand, they have specifically pleaded that it was petitioner who was responsible for MFA No.200653/2019 C/W causing the accident and by influencing the Police, he got filed a false complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, fanciful and without any basis and have sought for dismissal of the claim petitions.
11. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

12. In MVC No.57/2017, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-7.
13.
In MVC No.58/2017, petitioner has given evidence as PW-1.
He has examined the Doctor, who issued the disability certificate as PW-2.

He has got marked Ex.P-1 to P-14.
14.
Respondent No.2 has lead common evidence by examining one evidence as RW-1 and Exs.R-1 and R-2 are marked.
Ex.R-2 consist of 5 MFA No.200653/2019 C/W photographs of the offending vehicle and the auto rickshaw after the accident.

15. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions granting compensation in a sum of Rs.2,25,400/- with interest at 6% p.a. in MVC No.58/2017 and Rs.87,709/- with interest at 6% p.a. in MVC No.57/2017 and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.
The details of compensation granted are as under:
Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of income due to disability 1,83,600  Pain and sufferings 10,000  Food and nourishment 10,000  Traveling expenses 10,000  Loss of amenities 10,000
Medical expenses 1,800

Total 2,25,400  MFA No.200653/2019 C/W The Managing Director Neksrtc vs Umesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74940625/

sentences.text: As against the judgment and award in MVC No.58/2017, respondent No.2 has filed appeal in MFA No.200653/2019 contending that PW-2 who had issued the disability certificate is not a treated Doctor.
The Tribunal has erred in considering the whole body disability at 15% which is on the higher side.
Petitioner has not produced the driving licence either before the Tribunal or before the Investigating Officer.
At the time of alleged accident, the petitioner was driving auto rickshaw without any permit or insurance.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the higher side and prays to allow the appeal and either dismiss the petition or reduce the compensation.

17. Challenging the quantum of compensation granted in MVC No.58/2017 and seeking enhancement, petitioner has filed MFA Crob No.200001/2022 contending that the Tribunal has MFA No.200653/2019 C/W erred in considering the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.6,000/-.
The disability considered at 15% is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has also not considered 'loss of future prospects'.

The interest ought to have been granted at 9% p.a. and prays to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation.
18.

In MFA No.200652/2019, respondent No.2 has challenged the quantum of compensation granted for the damage caused to the auto rickshaw contending that the petitioner has not at all produced the estimation.
He has also not returned the damaged spare parts of the vehicle.
These aspects have not been properly appreciated by the Tribunal in granting compensation and prays to allow the appeal and dismiss the claim petition.
19. Heard arguments and perused the record.

Though respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by the petitioner, fact remains that in respect of the said accident,
complaint came to be lodged by the petitioner against respondent No.1 i.e., driver of the offending vehicle.
After completing the investigation, the investigating officer has filed the charge sheet against respondent No.1.
Admittedly, respondent No.1 has not challenged the charge sheet filed against him.
Consequently, the contention of respondents that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by the petitioner cannot be accepted.

21. On the other hand, the material placed on record, especially the complaint, FIR, charge sheet prove that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, petitioner sustained injuries.
MFA No.200653/2019 C/W 22.
As per the wound certificate at Ex.P-7, petitioner has suffered two injuries i.e., i) cut lacerated wound below left eye and swelling of nose The Managing Director Neksrtc vs Umesh And Anr

6 ii) cut lacerated wound and swelling over the right thigh.
X-ray reveal that there was fracture of distal end of both nasal bones and it is held to be grievous in nature.
23. PW-2 Doctor Yeshwant Dongre has issued the disability certificate.
He has calculated the disability at 60-70% of the affected part and 15-20% of the whole body.
Admittedly, he is not a treating Doctor.
During his cross examination, he has denied the suggestion that to help the petitioner, he has calculated the disability on the higher side.

Since PW-2 is not the treating Doctor and the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner is such that it is not going to affect his earning capacity, this Court is of the considered opinion that taking disability at 15% to MFA No.200653/2019 C/W the whole body is on the higher side.
Considering the nature of the job carried out by the petitioner and injuries suffered, this Court is of the considered opinion that it would be just and proper to take the disability at 10%.
24. As per the Aadhaar Card, the age of the petitioner was 27 years as on the date of the accident and therefore, the appropriate multiplier is 17.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has considered his notional income as Rs.6,000/- per month.
Since accident is of the year 2016, based on minimum wages, it would be appropriate to consider the notional income at Rs.8,750/- per month.

With these components, the compensation under the head "loss of income due to disability"
is Rs.8,750/- x 12 x 17 x 10% = 1,78,500/- as against Rs.1,83,600/- granted by the Tribunal.

MFA No.200653/2019 C/W 25. Looking to the nature of the injury suffered and the fact that it is has resulted in permanent partial disability, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the head 'Pain and suffering' and 'loss of amenities' is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.35,000/- and Rs.25,000/- respectively.
However, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the head 'food and nourishment' and 'traveling expenses', requires no interference.

26. Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,800/-
under the head 'Medical expenses'.
It also requires no interference.
27. The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered, it would be reasonable to expect that MFA No.200653/2019 C/W petitioner was under treatment atleast for a period of two months.

Therefore at the rate of Rs.8,750/- for a period of two months, petitioner is entitled to compensation in a sum of Rs.17,500/-.
28.
Thus in all, petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.2,77,800/- as against Rs.2,25,400/- granted by the Tribunal.
Of course, he is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

The details of the compensation is as detailed below:

Having regard to the fact that the compensation granted is enhanced, the appeal filed by the petitioner is allowed and one filed by respondent No.2 is rejected.
30. Now coming to the compensation granted for the damages caused to the auto rickshaw.
Based on the estimation at Ex.P-7, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.87,709/-.

However, petitioner has not produced the survey report, bills for having purchased new spare parts,
list of old spare parts returned, photographs taken by the surveyor before and after the repair and also the charges paid for actual repair work.
Respondent No.2 has taken up specific contention that the petitioner has got the compensation for repair of the auto rickshaw from its insurer.

The fact that the petitioner has not chosen to produce the original bills for having purchased the spare parts and also having paid the repair charges MFA No.200653/2019 C/W and other documents, it creates doubt as to whether the petitioner has actually undertaken the repair of the auto rickshaw or it supports the contention of respondent No.2 that in all probabilities, the petitioner has got the compensation from its insurer.
In the absence of supporting documents, only based on the estimation, the Tribunal has erred in granting compensation to the petitioner for the alleged repair carried out to the auto rickshaw.

In the result, appeal filed by respondent No.2 challenging the grant of compensation for the vehicle damages is liable to be set aside and consequently, allow the appeal filed by respondent No.2.
31.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No. 200653/2019 filed by the respondent No.2 is rejected.
MFA No.200653/2019 C/W (ii) MFA.Crob.No.200001/2022 filed by the petitioner is allowed.

The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the same with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization (minus the amount already paid/deposited) within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
